findings.location: source.html paragraph: "Some people in our churches who are drifting towards the world have perfected a feel-good gospel."
findings.source_quote: Some people in our churches who are drifting towards the world have perfected a feel-good gospel.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a more idiomatic Russian rendering that preserves the evaluative sense of "feel-good gospel" (an upbeat, consoling version of the gospel that lacks biblical seriousness). For example: «Некоторые в наших общинах, тянущиеся к миру, довели до совершенства «утешительное» или «приятное» Евангелие.»
findings.translation_quote: Некоторые в наших общинах, которые тянутся к миру, усовершенствовали благостную евангелие.

findings.location: source.html paragraph: "a woman of the church dressed with a cape dress that is form-fitting, and with a little covering hanging skimpily on the back of her head?"
findings.source_quote: a woman of the church dressed with a cape dress that is form-fitting, and with a little covering hanging skimpily on the back of her head?
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the clothing term to better match the original nuance. "Cape dress" denotes a modest dress with a cape/covering; current «платье с капюшоном» can imply a hooded garment. Suggested wording: «платье с накидкой, облегающее фигуру, и с небольшой покрывалкой, небрежно свисающей на затылке».
findings.translation_quote: женщина из церкви в платье с капюшоном, которое облегает фигуру, и с небольшой покрывалкой, небрежно повисшей на затылке?
